claim: Under Apple's EU DMA alternative business terms, developers kept App Store prices the same or increased them on 91% of products despite an average 10-percentage-point commission cut.
stance_target: speed/magnitude of App Store commission erosion under DMA alternative terms
scope_conditions: EU App Store storefronts, developers who enrolled in alternative business terms March-September 2024, 3-month before/after windows
quoted_support: developers who enrolled in Apple's alternative business terms kept prices the same, or increased them, on 9 out of every 10 products.

claim: 86% of the EUR20.1 million in commission savings generated by DMA alternative business terms flowed to developers based outside the EU, not to EU consumers or EU-domiciled developers.
stance_target: who captures value from DMA-mandated commission cuts
scope_conditions: EU App Store transactions, March-September 2024 enrollment cohorts
quoted_support: Of the EUR20.1 million reduction in commission fees, over 86% went to non-EU developers.

claim: A placebo test comparing a fake September 2023 enrollment date to the real September 2024 enrollment found a similar baseline rate of price decreases (4% vs 7%), suggesting most observed post-enrollment price decreases are not caused by the commission-rate cut.
stance_target: claim that DMA fee cuts are meaningfully passed through to EU consumers as lower prices
quoted_support: the price of 4% of the products decreased following the placebo enrollment, compared to 7% following actual enrollment in September 2024. The small difference suggests the bulk of the observed price decreases after enrollment are unrelated to the reduction in commission rates.

claim: This study was funded by Apple and authored by an Analysis Group VP; it measures consumer price pass-through of the alternative business terms fee schedule, not the adoption or usage share of third-party alternative app marketplaces, and is silent on marketplace install/download rates.
stance_target: whether Apple's commissioned DMA study answers the alternative-marketplace-adoption-rate question
scope_conditions: study scope explicitly limited to App Store storefront transactions; footnote 2 states it excludes web and other alternative marketplaces
quoted_support: This study is limited to transactions on the App Store and does not analyze prices on the web or other potential alternative marketplaces.
